- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early 30d window (first 5–7 days) after sentiment shift; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to early forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.25, -1.00, +1.00), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
- When true outcome deviates >+3% from 30d mean, model often fails to correct; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
